caption:
When I design mountain biking routes in Costa Rica, I always remind my guests that the topography doesn't care about your gears. There are ridges in our cloud forests so steep they turn even the strongest riders into hikers for a moment, forcing a slower, more deliberate connection with the landscape. I've scouted these climbs myself, feeling the damp grass underfoot and the thin air in my lungs, and I know that pushing your bike is simply part of the ritual. It is precisely these hard-earned transitions that make the descent feel like a gift.
